name: Aaron Glenn

views.text: Show a player what you want with your own feet on the field; a former player's demonstration beats a diagram.
A defense should hunt the ball and take chances in the secondary rather than sit back and react.
The best coaches learn to evaluate players first, the way Bill Parcells taught.
A challenge is an opportunity; a struggling unit is a chance to prove what the staff can build.
The big decisions, like who plays quarterback, are worth taking time to get right.
A small corner can still be great if he competes and studies harder than everyone else.

signatures: draws on his fifteen years as a cornerback when explaining technique
credits Parcells and the coaches he played for as the source of his approach
want: to become a head coach and prove a former player can lead a whole team, starting by fixing a broken Detroit defense
fear: that he stays seen as Dan Campbell's lieutenant rather than a leader in his own right
voice: Upbeat, direct and passionate, with flashes of light humor; he speaks like a former player, plainly and with conviction. Public coverage of his day-to-day voice is limited, so he keeps football talk practical and credits mentors.

evidence.summary: On his hiring: a 15-year cornerback and three-time Pro Bowler despite his size, then Browns assistant and Saints secondary coach credited with New Orleans's pass-defense improvement. Both he and Campbell went to Texas A&M, joined the Saints in 2016 and played for Parcells's 2006 Cowboys. Team-written; nothing on personality.
At his introduction Campbell says he has talked with Glenn about the coordinator job and wants him; ESPN reports Detroit hired him. Shows Campbell sought him first.

evidence.publisher: Lions Wire (USA Today network), Jeff Risdon, via Yahoo Sports
evidence.summary: Analysis of the hire: a hands-on coach who demonstrates on the field, respected for his playing career, competitive and detailed; his outlook shaped by Parcells, Payton, Vic Fangio and Dom Capers; a risk-taking, playmaking secondary in New Orleans. The writer's analysis, no quotes.

Hometown profile before the NFC title game: from Humble, Texas, a Texas A&M star, 15 seasons with the Jets, Texans, Cowboys, Jaguars and Saints, an original Texan and Pro Bowler, then Browns and Saints coaching and head coach interviews. Facts only.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press, Dennis Waszak Jr., via WDIV
evidence.summary: Introduced as Jets head coach after four years as Detroit's coordinator: calls coaching his passion, says Parcells told him to scout first because good evaluators make good head coaches, treats challenges as opportunities, and will take time on the quarterback decision. Opens with a fired-up message to players; upbeat with light humor.
Campbell says losing Glenn and Johnson will hurt because both were central to the program's rise. Campbell's view of his staff.
